barracuda.tested:
── Barracuda ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
No entry existed for "barracuda" - get_profile()/get_profile_key() silently fell
through to GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE (disk_bus="virtio", 512MB RAM cap). The on-disk
image (barracuda-fw8, id 97396424-2590-4473-b119-9763441a38b1) is IDE-formatted,
so virtio meant the guest never saw a bootable disk; separately, the 512MB cap is
under Barracuda CloudGen NGFW's real footprint - live-observed the node sitting at
563/512 MB (110% of cap) under the hypervisor's soft RAM ceiling. Same class of gap
already fixed once for "esxi" above (2026-07-18) and "isrv"/"titanium" before that.

reasons.min_ram_mb:
min_ram_mb=4096 matches Cisco's own documented CSR1000v IOS-XE 17.3 minimum (1/2/4
vCPU configs all list 4GB RAM as the floor - Cisco CSR1000v release notes). But
default_ram_mb was set equal to that floor, giving the launched VM zero headroom
above the bare minimum - live-observed 2026-07-21 (config-lifecycle sweep, round 7):
3 different csr1000vng-universalk9 instances all climbed to 100% of the 4096MB cap
and sat there for 3+ minutes before host-guard's hang-watchdog killed them for 0%
CPU (a real hang under memory pressure, not a slow-but-progressing boot - the
watchdog only fires on zero forward progress). 3 OTHER csr1000v/csr1000vng
instances in the same catalog HAD already passed earlier under lighter host load -
consistent with a device running exactly at its bare floor tipping over under real
hypervisor overhead + host contention, not a deterministic per-image failure.
default_ram_mb raised to 6144 (1.5x the floor) for real working margin, matching
this file's own pattern elsewhere (default set meaningfully above min, e.g.
barracuda/pfsense) - min_ram_mb stays at Cisco's documented 4096 floor, unchanged.

reasons.config_console:
Citrix SD-WAN never presents a command line on its
console - measured, not assumed. 25 minutes after a full boot the serial log
ended at kernel time 48.68s and the VGA framebuffer (read over RFB) showed the
SAME frozen text, with none of the newlines/`admin`/`help` we sent appearing on
it, i.e. the guest processed no input at all. EVE-NG agrees by omission: none of
its 30 config_*.py scripts covers ctxsdw. The console itself stays "telnet" and
still works for watching the boot - only CONFIG read/write is refused, and it is
refused with this reason instead of a misleading "no dialect for vendor citrix"
(the same vendor's nsvpx has a full working dialect). Delete these two keys if a
future build offers a console login; nothing else has to change.

iosv.tested:
Bare "iosv-*" image folder format (no "cisco-" prefix) - some real IOSv uploads use
this naming instead of "cisco-iosv-*". Found missing 2026-07-22 (the project owner: "How hard can
it be to categorise those IOL images properly?") chasing a live failure: image
"iosv-159-3-m6" had NO profile match at all (get_profile_key returned None), so it fell
through to GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE's 120s boot_timeout_sec and got none of the extended
busy-console retry treatment node_config._retry_deadline_s gives any profiled device -
it was still running the original fixed-2-attempt budget the whole night. Same specs as
"cisco-iosv" above (identical underlying software, just a different upload naming
convention) - see that entry's comment for the 400s boot_timeout_sec evidence.

reasons.day0_channel:
ISRv is IOS-XE, same family as csr1000v/cat8000v - CvacChannel's own
docstring explicitly names it in scope ("CSR1000v, ISRv, Catalyst 8000v,
cat9kv"), and Cisco documents CSR1000v + ISRv together in one Software
Configuration Guide (see this profile's own comment above). Tagged
2026-07-28 to complete the CVAC family started with csr1000v.

isrv.tested:
ISRv (Integrated Services Virtual Router) - same IOS-XE family as CSR1000v,
documented together in Cisco's own "CSR 1000v and Cisco ISRv Software
Configuration Guide". Had no entry here before 2026-07-12 - unmatched image
names fall through to GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE (512MB/1cpu), which is nowhere near
enough: first-boot crypto keygen + package extraction under that much memory
pressure crash-loops (repeated "Failed to format /dev/vdaN. Rebooting."),
easily misread as a broken image (same failure shape as the dynamips
out-of-range-RAM SIGSEGV found the same day - see DYNAMIPS_MAX_RAM_MB above).
4096MB/2cpu mirrors this table's existing csr1000v entry (same vendor family
minimum); EVE-NG's own isrv-17.03.02 howto independently confirms 4096MB is
the correct order of magnitude (they run 1 vCPU/4096MB for a lighter profile).
default_ram_mb is 6144, not 4096 (2026-07-21, re-applied 2026-07-23 - see that date's
commit for why): same fix and same reason as the sibling csr1000v entry above (both
are Cisco IOS-XE platforms, documented together in Cisco's own "CSR1000v and ISRv
Software Configuration Guide"): min_ram_mb==default_ram_mb left zero real-world
headroom above the bare floor. Live-observed 2026-07-21 (config-lifecycle sweep round
8): 2 different isrv instances (isrv-21e32d3e, isrv-ucmk9-0beacd55) both climbed to
97-100% of the 4096MB cap and sat there for 4.5+ minutes - the same "hung under memory
pressure" signature already root-caused for csr1000v. min_ram_mb stays at 4096,
unchanged. RE-CONFIRMED live 2026-07-23: a bulk catalog-regeneration commit
(309ff0f7, "populate the 73 EVE-NG-template gaps") silently reverted this same fix
back to 4096/4096 without anyone noticing, re-exposing the exact same OOM-hang this
entry already fixed once - caught only because a live sweep hit isrv again and this
RAM value was the first thing checked. If you're regenerating/bulk-populating this
table from a template, please diff against evidence-backed comments like this one
first - a template regen has no way to know a manually-tuned value came from a real,
reproduced incident.

past the GRUB menu after 5.5+ minutes (0 bytes of further serial output,

under memory pressure). The identical image at -m 4096 -smp 2 reached a full

silently gets the 512MB generic floor" failure class already fixed for isrv/
NX-OS/FortiGate above (see those comments) - min/default set from the PROVEN
4096MB/2-vCPU boot, not a vendor-doc guess.

reasons.boot_timeout_sec:
SONiC's own native profile (sonic-vs, below) already needs 300s; SONiC +
vrnetlab's nested-QEMU/health-probe overhead (mikrotik's +60s pattern)
budgets more.
reasons.image:
dell/dell_sonic/Makefile's own comment: a file named "dell-sonic-4.2.1.qcow2"
builds "vrnetlab/dell_sonic:4.2.1" - that exact example version used verbatim.

reasons.image:
ipinfusion/ocnos/Makefile via the standard IMG_REPOSITORY=$(REGISTRY)$(IMG_VENDOR)_$(IMG_NAME)
rule (VENDOR=IPInfusion, NAME=OcNOS -> lowercased "ipinfusion_ocnos").
Version "6.5.2-101" is the version the vrnetlab README itself documents as
"Tested booting and responding to Telnet" (README's own real evidence).
reasons.min_ram_mb: README "System requirements": CPU 2 core, RAM <4GB, Disk <4GB.

reasons.boot_timeout_sec:
vrnetlab's own /health readiness probe (0 running) gates the container's
entrypoint until the nested VM has actually booted RouterOS - budget more
than the bare-qcow2 CHR's 60s for the extra nested-boot + wrapper overhead.

reasons.min_ram_mb:
README "Host requirements": 4 vCPU, 6 GB RAM. NOT a router/switch/firewall -
CMG Linux is a DB/control VM component of Nokia's MAG-C mobile-core platform,
boots via cloud-init (not a CLI day-0 flow), console is a real Linux login
(user "clab", vrnetlab-injected password) once cloud-init completes.

reasons.image:
plvision/plvision_sonic/Makefile via the standard IMG_REPOSITORY rule
(VENDOR=PLVision, NAME=sonic -> "plvision_sonic"). Version
"lite_1_13_202405" is the Makefile's own worked example
("plvision_sonic-vs-lite_1_13_202405.qcow2" -> that exact tag).
reasons.min_ram_mb: README "System requirements": CPU 2 cores, RAM 4GB, DISK ~6.5GB.

reasons.boot_timeout_sec:
README: "wait for the 'Startup Completed' message... then rebooted to fully
apply the configuration" - a two-phase boot, budget generously.
reasons.image:
spirent/vstc/Makefile via the standard IMG_REPOSITORY rule (VENDOR=Spirent,
NAME=vstc -> "spirent_vstc"). Version "5.55.3216" is the vrnetlab README's
own worked topology example.
reasons.min_ram_mb:
No explicit "System requirements" section in the vrnetlab README for this
kind - it is a real traffic-generation/test appliance (Spirent Virtual Test
Center), same functional category as netplex's existing native
"test-traffic-ostinato"/"test-traffic-trex" taxonomy entries; sized like
those (2 vCPU / 4GB is the documented floor for the *other* vrnetlab test
tool README that DOES state one, ipinfusion/ocnos, used here as the nearest
comparable-class floor rather than an invented number). Default credentials
per README: admin / spt_admin. eth0 reserved for vrnetlab mgmt (generic
rule), data ports eth1+ used for actual test-generated traffic.

xrv9k.tested:
ROOT CAUSE (2026-07-18, device audit for image "xrv9k-fullk9"): get_profile()
only matches when the normalized image name CONTAINS the normalized key, and
the real catalog image is imported as "xrv9k-fullk9" (folder name, no "cisco-"
prefix) - it never contained "cisco-xrv9k", so it silently fell through to
GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE (512 MB RAM / 1 vCPU / 120s boot_timeout / machine=pc)
instead of this profile's 16 GB / 2 vCPU / 900s / machine=q35. A real XRv9k
image cannot even start IOS XR's control plane with 512 MB RAM, so every boot
guaranteed-failed. "csr1000v"/"asav" already carry this same bare-key duplicate
alongside their "cisco-*" key (see below) for exactly this reason - do the same
here so any "xrv9k*"-named image (with or without a vendor prefix) matches.
